prompt:
Create pixel-art pieces for a modern 16-bit-style top-down RPG town map (three-quarter overhead view, like a classic SNES JRPG town).

Image 1 is a PLACEMENT GUIDE on a magenta page: fill each grey box edge to edge with the piece described for it. Do not copy the grey colour.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: the approved walking sprite of a character from this game at the same pixel scale as the map (about 90 sprite pixels tall). Match its sprite-pixel size, its outlines and its flat 2-3 tone shading with light from the upper left.

Image 3 is approved art from this same game map: match its colours, outline weight and shading exactly.
Image 4 is approved art from this same game map: match its colours, outline weight and shading exactly.

Pieces:
- the top-left box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). a dense forest seen from straight above: many round dark-green tree crowns packed together, with lighter green tops lit from the upper left and dark shadows between them, evenly spread.
- the top-centre box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). rugged rocky mountain ground seen from above: grey-brown rock with sharp ridges, cracks and darker crevices, a few light highlights, evenly spread, no snow.
- the middle-left box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). pale golden beach sand seen from above with fine ripples and a few tiny pebbles, evenly spread.
- the middle-centre box (96x96 sprite pixels): a SEAMLESS texture (left edge continues into the right edge, top into bottom). deep blue sea water seen from above with small white-capped wave marks and darker blue patches, evenly spread, no shore.

Draw each piece as one continuous picture with no lines dividing it into squares. Render as true pixel art: every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur. Between the boxes: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF), no text.
